newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria hopes UN will compensate for Yugo embargo.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria hopes UN will compensate for Yugo embargo.

text.p: Bulgaria, hit by a deep economic crisis, said on Monday it relied on the United Nations to compensate it for the losses it suffered from the international embargo on neighbouring Yugoslavia.

A draft resolution expected to be passed this week calls for economic help for countries affected by the embargo and stresses the need for practical measures to mitigate the long-term negative impact of the sanctions, said the head of the foreign ministry foreign economy department, Maya Dobreva.
"Bulgaria has introduced in the U.N. General Assembly a draft resolution aimed at offsetting losses sustained by third countries during the war in ex-Yugoslavia," she told reporters.

"We expect the U.N. member countries to pass the resolution by consensus and provide urgent economic assistance to the states affected by the strict implementation of the sanctions against neighbouring rump Yugoslavia," Dobreva said.
She said the resolution had widespread support from European countries, the United States and other members.

"We don't expect direct funding, but the country could be compensated through participation in post-war reconstruction projects in ex-Yugoslavia, funded by international organisations," Dobreva added.
Estimating Bulgaria's losses from the embargo is difficult, but the government's sanctions committee put the figure at between $7 billion and $9 billion.

The Balkan country, which shares a 250-mile (400 km) border with ex-Yugoslavia and whose road and and rail links to Europe pass through Serbia, was practically cut off from European markets by the trade embargo during the conflict.
The U.N. Security Council suspended sanctions against Belgrade in November 1995 at the time of the Dayton peace accord.
